newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra to pay FIM 445 mln to Fincantieri.
newsitem.headline: Metra to pay FIM 445 mln to Fincantieri.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab said on Wednesday it had signed a planned agreement with Italy's Fincantieri to merge diesel activities and would pay 445 million markka in cash to Fincantieri in the deal.
"Metra will initially have a 87.8 percent and Fincantieri a 12.2 percent holding in the merged company to be named Wartsila NSD Corporation," Metra said in a statement.
"As part of the transaction Metra will pay a cash consideration of 445 million markka to Fincantieri," it said.

Metra last September first revealed a tentative deal to merge its diesel unit with Fincantieri, and said on Wednesday the agreement was still subject to approval by competition authorities after which the new unit would start operations.

Wartsila NSD will comprise Wartsila Diesel, New Sulzer Diesel and Diesel Ricerche, and initially a 40 percent holding in Fincantieri's diesel engine division Grandi Motori Trieste, which has been incorporated as a separate company.
"This shareholding will increase gradually," Metra said. "Simultaneously Fincantieri's holding in Wartsila NSD Corporation will increase up to 15.4 percent."

The board of the new firm, to be the largest in its field worldwide, will be chaired by Metra President and CEO George Ehrnrooth, and its president and CEO will be Wartsila Diesle Group's CEO Pentti-Juhani Hintikka, Metra said.
After the deal, diesel operations will make up about 80 percent of Metra's 11 billion markka annual sales which also include bathroom ceramics and speciality steel products.
Metra has said the deal would be neutral for 1996-97 earnings with a positive impact thereafter.
Fincantieri is controlled by giant Italian state holding company Istituto per la Ricostruzione Industriale (IRI).
